brand.name: Signet Artists
brand._tagline_note: REWRITTEN 2026-08-17. Was 'PROfessional PERFORMANCE FOR PROFESSIONAL SETTINGS'. The capitalisation read as a typo at display size and the sentence said nothing a planner could act on. This is the h1 on the home page and nowhere else, set in the display face at uppercase, so it has a hard length budget: the retired line was 47 characters and ran three lines. Anything much past that fills the first screen on its own and pushes the lede and both buttons under the fold. The rest of the offer moved into `intro` below.
brand._intro_note: REWRITTEN 2026-08-17 with the Q4 refocus. The old version sold the 2027 system, 'from a single DJ to a 13 piece band', which is not the product. It also carried three of the copy bugs from the 17 Aug audit. This renders as the home page hero lede and as the MusicGroup description in schema, so it has to stand alone. AMENDED 2026-09-04: the clause 'and our rates published right on the website' was removed with the no-published-price decision. It was the one sentence on the site that made the claim in Daniel's own words, and it had stopped being true. Nothing else in the intro moved, and the hero was not touched.
brand.intro: Signet Artists delivers live entertainment for private events in Denver, Colorado and surrounding areas. All provided in a variety of genres and configurations - effortlessly.
brand._phone_note: Decided 2026-08-01: no phone number is published. Email is the only published route. If that changes, restore the markup in the footer partial, the contact page and the home page close section.
brand.serviceArea: Denver, BOULDER, and the mountain corridor

brand._formsubmit_note: FormSubmit's hashed endpoint for hello@signetartists.com, so the address is not in the page source. Same pattern as daniel-fox.com and danielchristopherfox.com. The plain address still renders on the contact page, deliberately.
brand._forms_note: ADDED 2026-09-20. The two Google Forms behind /for-artists/ (act submission) and /preferred-vendors/join/ (vendor application), owned by danielchristopherfox@gmail.com, each linked to its own sheet. llms.about: {name} is a live music company for private events in {serviceArea}. No prices are published. What the pricing page carries is what live music costs in the Colorado market, each price with the source it came from, and Signet prices a specific night when the date is sent.
llms.videos: Each clip the roster plays has its own page. {site}/video/ lists them all by act, and so does {site}/video-sitemap.xml.
llms.actsNote: All acts and configurations are subject to availability.
pricing: {name} publishes no price list, no starting prices and no hourly prices. Actual prices vary by date, size, hours and location. {site}/pricing/ sets out what live music costs in the Colorado market, with each price attributed to the public source it came from, so a reader can set a budget before writing to Signet. To get the number for a specific night, send the date: {site}/contact/
Travel beyond the Denver metro area, a night's lodging past the passes, holiday weekends and New Year's Eve are priced with the date.

_comment: Every brand-dependent value on the site. No template hardcodes one. Values in [square brackets] are unresolved and render with a dotted underline in the browser so open decisions stay visible while browsing.
_images_note: PLACEHOLDERS. Free-licence Unsplash stills, cropped 16:9 and duotoned into the brand palette so they read as one art-directed set rather than five unrelated stock photos. Deliberately objects, gear and empty rooms — no people, and nothing that implies it is our band. Swap every one of these for footage from the shoot; the alt text will need rewriting too.
_acts_moved_note: The two house bands (The Standards, The Headliners) and the DJ lived here until the 2026-08-15 restructure. The business books named acts, so the roster moved to _src/data/acts.json with a real schema: bucket and config tags, per-config pricing read off the rate card, and flagship/listing status. Nothing reads site.acts any more.
_players_removed_note: Bandleader bios (Daniel Fox, Tejas Singh) lived here from 2026-08-07 until the 2026-08-15 restructure. The restructure spec bans player names and lineup detail outright: acts and faces only. A bio framed as the chair a person holds in the house band is exactly the framing being retired. Faces carry the same trust load now, from acts.json, on the act pages and the roster cards. This reverses the 2026-08-07 instruction to publish names, so if the spec is wrong on that point the bios are recoverable from git history.
_configurations_note: DRAFT 2026-08-07, swept 2026-08-17 with the Q4 refocus: rows now cover exactly what is sold, solo through quartet plus the DJ. The quintet, seven-, ten- and thirteen-piece rows are in git history if a larger size ever returns as a sold product. Solo has no call-out/hourly row in `rates` (the card publishes it as a range only), so it appears here for logistics without a rates twin; every other row name stays locked to `rates` so the technical page and the rate card cannot disagree. A solo's logistics mirror the DJ's: one person and a small PA. Footprints are the working figures a band actually takes, not the stage-rental guidance, which runs far larger; that gap is the point of the page. Inputs are channel counts at the desk, including one announcement mic on its own channel.
_configurations_provisional_note: Draws the brass edge down the technical page tables (styles.css .table-scroll[data-provisional]). Set to false once Daniel's correction pass lands and these stop being our own inference.
_corporateShapes_note: ADDED 2026-08-17 with the Q4 refocus. The three shapes a corporate enquiry actually arrives as, for the /corporate/ page. Act and config are ids so the act name and the configuration label resolve out of acts.json rather than being retyped. The two price columns were removed 2026-09-04: the cards carry the shape and the build, and the number for a date comes from checking the date.
_credits_note: ADDED 2026-09-03, from Daniel's list of the companies, institutions and venues the roster's artists have played for. Rendered by build.py credits() as the one-colour logo strip on the home page and /corporate/, and as a Credits line in llms.txt. Each logo ships as img/logos/<id>.svg, normalised to currentColor (provenance in img/logos/SOURCES.md); `h` scales a mark against the strip's base height so a stacked crest and a wide wordmark carry the same visual weight. The ten with logos: national employers, the museum, the two hotel flags, a major-league club, and the two Colorado names Daniel added the same day, Casa Bonita and Monarch (Daniel's call 2026-09-03, which supersedes the acts.json footage note that left the casino unnamed). The club stages and the rest are the `also` sentence, text only and home page only. Held back: the Hummingbird bar. Label 'Trusted and booked by' is Daniel's wording, 2026-09-03.
_eventTypes_note: RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-20 with the SEO buildout. Each tag is now a doorway into its occasion page, which is the home page's placement for the occasion tree. 'Weddings' became 'Wedding cocktail hours' deliberately: the cocktail hour is the one wedding product in 2026 scope, and the tag should not promise a reception band that does not exist yet. Galas route to the corporate hub, where they are framed at small-format scale per the 17 Aug audit.
_plannerFaqs_note: DRAFT 2026-08-07. The deep operational FAQ, the questions a planner asks that are not about price. `faqs` above stays the short pricing set on the pricing page; this is the full set on planners/faq/. Any entry with "open": true is an answer written as a best guess because it is a business policy nobody has decided yet. Those render with a dotted underline, the same convention as an unresolved brand value, so an undecided policy cannot ship silently. Resolve them, drop the flag.
_plannerFaqs_reconciliation: Reconciled against the contract drafts in outreach/readiness/ before planner outreach, 16 to 17 Aug 2026. ALL SEVEN OPEN FLAGS ARE NOW CLOSED. Closed against the contract: what holds a date (§3), balance and payment (§3 plus invoice format 03c), outdoors (§7). Closed by Daniel 17 Aug: showcases (no, and no public dates either, these are private groups), dress code (ratified as written), green room and meals (neither required, so they do NOT enter contract §7), and the cancellation window at 90 days. The cancellation entry was the important one: the site had been contradicting contract §5 outright. Vocabulary is the contract's throughout: deposit, never retainer. Anything reopened here must be reopened in 03a at the same time, because these answers and that document are now the same policy in two registers.
_rates_removed_note: REMOVED 2026-09-04. `rates` held the call-out plus hourly table and `_rates_byRequest_note` explained the by-request rows. The site publishes no Signet price of any kind from that date, and the repo is the published site, so the numbers left the data file with the copy. They live in OFFER.md, which is the internal model and always was. Do not restore them here: market figures go in market-rates.json with their provenance, and Signet's own numbers go in a quote.
_extras_note: REWRITTEN 2026-09-04 with the no-published-price decision. This was an item plus a `rate` column and rendered as a priced table. It is now the list of what is itemised separately on a quote, which is a real and useful thing to publish, with no figure attached to any line. The figures are in OFFER.md.
_insurance_removed_note: REMOVED 2026-09-04. Held the general-liability limits and rendered them through {{gl_per_occurrence}} / {{gl_aggregate}} on /planners/ and /corporate/client-dinners/. The coverage is real and unchanged; the figures came off because the no-published-figure rule of 2026-09-04 is written as an absolute and the repo is the published site. The copy now says the certificate names the venue as additional insured and meets what Colorado venues write into their vendor requirements. The limits are in OFFER.md and on the certificate itself.
_faqs_note: REWRITTEN 2026-09-04 with the no-published-price decision. These are the pricing page's questions and they still answer the money question, with the market's figures instead of Signet's. Figures only ever arrive here as {{market:<id>}} tokens off market-rates.json; a page that resolves one has to carry {{market_sources}} or the build fails. Never type a figure into an answer.
